title: Transport of ordinary scalar tensor and line comparison
statement: Let C be a category with object universe c and morphism universe v, and J a Grothendieck topology with module sheafification in universe max(c,v) and the usual locally-bijective characterization. Let alpha : R → T be a morphism of commutative ring sheaves. Use the actual sheaf tensor, scalar extension and tensor sections [def-sp-scalar-tensor-comparison-data]. Let F be an ordinary scalar functor whose specified object equalities identify F(M) with changeOfRings(alpha,M) and whose maps are the corresponding transported scalar-extension maps. Let t(M,U,s,x) be precisely the sheafification-unit image of s tensor x transported back along that object equality. Let N be an R-module sheaf, P a T-module sheaf, B : F(N) ≅ P, and c_U a family of underlying functions N(U) → P(U) such that B(t(N,U,1,y)) = c_U(y). Then there is exactly one natural isomorphism b : F(- tensor N) ≅ F(-) tensor P such that b_M(t(M tensor N,U,s,x tensor y)) = t(M,U,s,x) tensor c_U(y) on every object and every pure tensor. No invertibility of N or P is required.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict and section-tensor-product (03EK, 03EL); explicit transport/extensionality consequence used in the coefficient-twist scalar construction.

proof.text: The specified object equalities, followed by the ordinary-to-universe scalar-extension isomorphism, give a natural isomorphism e from F to the sheafified scalar tensor functor G. Naturality follows by the hypothesis on F.map. The tensor-section identification follows from the naturality of the sheafification unit.

Use the normalized binary scalar comparison to identify G(M tensor N) with G(M) tensor G(N). Tensor the second factor with e_N inverse followed by B. Conjugate this comparison by e to obtain b. Naturality follows from binary-comparison naturality and naturality of tensoring a second-factor map. The pure-tensor formula follows by applying the two comparison formulas and cancelling e with its inverse.

For a competing b, evaluate after e inverse on scalar pure tensors. The specified section formula identifies both maps there. Scalar-extension tensor extensionality gives equality at every object M; natural-transformation extensionality and Iso.ext give equality of b.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryScalarTensorLineTransport
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v} RingCat.{max c v})]
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max c v}] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max c v}]
    {R T : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v}} (α : R ⟶ T)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max c v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{max c v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj T))
    (hF : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings α M)
    (hmF : ∀ {M M'} (f : M ⟶ M'), F.map f = eqToHom (hF M) ≫
      SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom α M f ≫ eqToHom (hF M').symm)
    (t : ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.{max c v}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))
      (U : Cᵒᵖ), T.obj.obj U → M.val.obj U → (F.obj M).val.obj U)
    (ht : ∀ M U s x, t M U s x = (eqToHom (hF M).symm).val.app U
      ((toSheafify J (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsPresheaf α M).presheaf).app U
        (s ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj U,(α.hom.app U).hom] x)))
    (N : SheafOfModules.{max c v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))
    (P : SheafOfModules.{max c v} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj T))
    (B : F.obj N ≅ P)
    (c : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, N.val.obj U → P.val.obj U)
    (hc : ∀ U y, B.hom.val.app U (t N U 1 y) = c U y) :
    ∃! b : SheafOfModules.siteSheafTensorRight N ⋙ F ≅
      F ⋙ SheafOfModules.siteSheafTensorRight P,
      ∀ M U s x y, (b.hom.app M).val.app U
          (t _ U s (SheafOfModules.siteSheafTensorTmul M N U x y)) =
        SheafOfModules.siteSheafTensorTmul (F.obj M) P U
          (t M U s x)
          (c U y)
